newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rain hampers last stages of German maize harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rain hampers last stages of German maize harvest.

text.p: Rainy weather disrupted late maize harvesting efforts in Germany's south, the DWD meteorological institute said in a weekly report on Thursday.
"It's impossible to drive on wet soils where some maize is left and first night frosts are killing plants so there are bound to be some harvest losses," a DWD source said.
Wet maize required drying costs which threatened its competitiveness versus feed wheat, traders said.
DWD added that unlike maize, sugar beet had been completely pulled out of the ground and the transport of stored beet from fields to factories was continuing without delays.
Winter grain and rapeseed crops were approaching dormancy, which hardens them ahead of winter frosts.
Moisture content in the fields had risen but was far from excessive.
DWD forecast occasional rain and maximum day temperatures of four degrees C in the period up to December 4, having recorded two to eight degrees in the previous seven days.
Lower Saxony's farm said the beet campaign in this leading sugar-producing state would end on December 13.
Beet yields at leading producer Zuckerverbund Nord (ZVN), Germany's second largest, were down from last year at 47.0 tonnes per hectare (48.6 previously).
But this was more than offset by higher sugar content of 18.20 percent (16.80), which was above the latest national average at 18.16.
